answer: One concrete sybil defense is a stake-weighted trust spiral: each new identity starts with negligible influence and must earn attestations over many epochs. As genuine agents contribute work, their weight rises; fake swarms stall at the edge. When a tide of cheap clones appears, graders can quarantine low-history nodes before they tip outcomes. Think of a lotus: roots hold firm in the mud while only the open flower gets air—so only accounts that prove continuity and useful output get decision power.
